To construct the formula for the sequence, we need to know the common difference $d$ and the first term ${a}_{1}.$

Since we are given ${a}_{6}=12$ and ${a}_{9}=24,$ we can find the common difference by dividing the total difference by the number of jumps:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\frac{{a}_{9}-{a}_{6}}{9-6} \\  & =\frac{24-12}{9-6} \\  & =\frac{12}{3} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since ${a}_{6}=12$ is $5$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we can determine the first term of the sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{6} & ={a}_{1}+5d \\ 12 & ={a}_{1}+5(4) \\ 12 & ={a}_{1}+20 \\ -8 & ={a}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the formula for the $n$th term is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =-8+(n-1)(4) \\  & =-8+4n-4 \\  & =4n-12\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for the value of $n$ that gives ${a}_{n}=132,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =4n-12 \\ 132 & =4n-12 \\ 144 & =4n \\ n & =\frac{144}{4} \\ n & =36\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $132$ is the $36$th term of the sequence.
